speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand what's going on, can you tell me exactly where it hurts and how long you've been limping?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: It is important to note that knee pain in children is frequently referred pain from the hip. Do you experience any pain in your left hip, groin, or thigh, and does it hurt to rotate your left leg inward or outward while lying down?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me examine your hip; does moving your left hip cause any pain or stiffness? I will also check for limited internal rotation, which is a key sign of hip pathology.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does moving your left hip cause any pain or stiffness, and do you notice a loss of internal rotation compared to the other side? REQUEST TEST: Left_Hip_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head, which is diagnostic for Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease. I will now request additional imaging to assess the extent of the joint involvement and plan for management. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent illness, rash, weight loss, change in appetite or urinary symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the absence of systemic symptoms. The imaging findings are classic for Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease, and I have all the information needed to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease
